title: Ando emerges from stealth with $20M and an agent-native team chat aimed at Slack
subtitle: Accel, Index Ventures and Emergence Capital back a messaging platform where AI agents join channels as first-class members with persistent identity and shared context.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Ando launched publicly on September 24 with $20 million in combined pre-seed and seed funding — Accel led the pre-seed round; Index Ventures and Emergence Capital co-led the seed. Founder Sara Du described the product as a team messaging platform built from the ground up for humans and AI agents to work together. Agents in Ando join channels, threads and its live conversation format ('Jams') with their own identity, permissions and persistent memory, and the platform is intentionally agent-agnostic — teams can plug in Codex, Claude, Grokbot and others rather than being locked to one lab. The company says active users are spread across roughly a dozen countries, mostly in software, real estate and financial services.

What Ando is really selling is the identity model. Today, when an agent operates inside a Slack or a Teams workspace, it wears a webhook or a bot user — it does not have a stable, persistent identity, and the workspace's audit log has no clean way to say 'this decision was made by that agent, in that thread, with these tools available.' Ando's bet is that once agents make more than a small fraction of workplace decisions, the pattern of a bot-shim shows its age. Give the agent an account, a permission scope, a message history, and a persistent memory of what it has been asked before, and the enterprise-security team gets something it can actually govern.

The Slack-comparison framing is convenient marketing but a strategic risk. Slack itself is not sitting still — Salesforce has been rewiring it around Agentforce for a year — and Microsoft Teams is pushing Copilot agents into the same seat. A new entrant that competes on 'agents are first-class citizens' has to be visibly better on that axis, and be at least tolerable on the boring parts (calls, notifications, search, integrations, mobile). Ando's willingness to keep a bridge to Slack, rather than force full migration, is the pragmatic move — the same one that let Notion and Linear grow inside teams that could not fully leave the incumbent.

Takeaway for learners: 'agents as team members' sounds like a UX pitch, but the design problem is really about permissions, memory and audit. If you are building anything agentic inside a workplace, sketch the identity layer before you sketch the chat interface — who the agent is when it acts, whose credentials it borrows, and what a compliance officer sees six months later when something went wrong. Every serious agent product converges on those three questions eventually.
